content: Magnesium hydroxide levels can be reduced by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but pazopanib and antacid dosing should be separated by several hours. Close monitoring is advised. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and administration should be separated by at least 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification is recommended, and administration of pexidartinib should be separated by at least 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. Close monitoring is advised. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the effects of intravenous potassium phosphates by cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium also reduces serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. Alternative therapies should be used if available. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of raltegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium-containing antacids lower raltegravir plasma levels when taken within 6 hours of the raltegravir dose. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is advised. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administration should be separated by at least 1 hour, and close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification is recommended, and close monitoring is advised. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the effects of intravenous sodium phosphates by cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium also reduces serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. Therapy modification is recommended, and alternatives should be used if available. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but there is a potential risk of alkalosis. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, sotorasib should be administered 4 hours before or 10 hours after the antacid. Spironolactone increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Streptomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tobramycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Torasemide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Triamterene increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, which reduces bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Vitamin D increases magnesium hydroxide levels by raising serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in patients with renal impairment. The combined use of vitamin D and magnesium-containing products should be avoided in patients with chronic renal failure. It should be used with caution in patients with renal insufficiency. Magnesium hydroxide is classified as pregnancy category A, meaning it is generally considered safe for use during pregnancy based on controlled studies showing no evidence of fetal risk. Its use in nursing mothers appears to be safe. The laxative effect of magnesium hydroxide typically occurs within 5 to 6 hours. It is excreted in the urine (up to 30% as absorbed magnesium) and feces (as unabsorbed drug). Copyright © 2010 First DataBank, Inc.
